data.claim: If the token budget is reserved atomically per-event before event generation begins, then exhaustion can only prevent the next event from starting—it can never interrupt an in-progress write. This makes every budget-exhaustion halt clean by construction, so resumption is always safe as long as the log's append-only identity is intact. The only refusal case is log corruption from causes other than budget exhaustion (hardware failure, concurrent writes). The cost is potential underutilization of the global budget pool and the need to estimate per-event token costs before generation.
